### How to prepare a set of Accounts

			Print

	Modified on: Wed, 10 Mar, 2021 at  5:01 PM

		Navigation - Accounts Production >> Client Dashboard >> Reports >> Annual Accounts >> Add New Report

Refer to the link

Help/Guide

Head to the accounts production module using the Navigation above and select a client to proceed with. Before preparing a set of accounts, you will need to do the following;

1. Create Accounting Period (if you haven't done so in Bookkeeping) - Settings > Accounting Periods

2. Add Directors - Settings > Report Settings > Company Contacts 

3. Import Trial Balance (Manually, CSV, Bookkeeping or Integrations) - Tasks > Trial Balance 

After importing the Trial Balance, you can then proceed to preparing the accounts. Head to Reports > Annual Accounts > 'Add New Report'. Fill the fields in accordingly as shown below, and most importantly, select the Trial Balance(s) you wish to use to prepare the accounts with, then click Generate.

To submit your final accounts, head to Tasks > Submit and click the + Submit Accounts button. Select the accounts you want to submit, you'll then have to go through the four steps to submit

These four process steps of submission are as follows:

Validate Report: Annual report so generated is to be validated here. If there are any errors, then the same will be listed here and you may click on resolve to resolve the errors.

After resolving the errors, you will be allowed to proceed to the next step.

Verify Report: Report so generated is displayed. You may preview the Report which is to be submitted to Companies House. Also if you want to navigate to the previous step, you may click on the ‘Previous’ tab.

Gateway Details: Here details of Companies House login are to be filled. 

Submit Accounts: Once you are logged in to Companies House all the accounts and reports to be submitted is to be reviewed and then submitted to Companies House.

The general settings is where you have the ability to change the format of your reports on a global level. This means that any changes that are done here will be reflected in all annual accounts created for your clients.

Editing the account reports for LLPs / Partnerships / Sole Traders

Select the type of company you would like to edit the annual accounts from the navigation panel. 

To edit the information, click on the blue button next to the section that needs to be changed.

You can edit the notes content by dragging and dropping the tags that need to be included and then save.

Editing the account reports for Limited Companies

Click on the 'Limited Company' drop down box in the navigation panel to select the accounts report need to be edited. 

Similar to editing the notes for LLPs, Partnerships and Sole Traders, click on the report that needs to be edited and then use the blue button to select the specific section. 

Adding accountants to your annual report

You can add accountants in the global settings which can then be selected in the accountants report when creating a set of annual accounts. 

To add an accountants, go into the accountants section in the navigation panel. 

Click on 'Add New' and fill in the details accordingly. 

When in the accountants report settings within a client specific account, you will be able to select the accountant that has just been created.

### Charts of Accounts

			Print

	Modified on: Mon, 12 Oct, 2020 at  5:35 PM

		Location: Accounts Production module > Settings > Charts of Accounts

It Displays the list of various accounts that are maintained with their codes that are inbuilt. The list of accounts showing the account name, type under which account is grouped with their codes. Actions that can be taken into accounts.

### Edit Account

You can edit the details related to the account using the Action drop-down. On editing, the Account Type and Account Code cannot be changed/edited.

### 

### Add Account

You may add a new account relating to Profit & Loss Account, by clicking on ‘+ Add Account’.

Select the account type under which the created account will be classified.

Account code is to be selected from the drop-down list, to give a code number to the created account.

VAT code is to be selected (if any) for the account from the drop-down list as applicable. Whether the account is to be kept active or saved as archive depends on your requirement. However, by default the account is active.

On saving the created account, it will be added to the list of the chart of accounts.

You can filter the accounts by specifying the code or account name.

Accounts can be filtered alphabetically, by selecting the alphabet all the accounts starting with that alphabet will be filtered and listed.

Accounts can be filtered according to its type. This can be done by the Status drop-down. There are two types:

Normal: To use this filter you will have to specify the account name in the text box. This will filter the respective account.

Archive: On selecting the archive all the accounts which are inactive and saved as archive will be displayed. The account can be un-archived by editing it and putting a tick on the active checkbox.

You may download the list of the chart of accounts in a PDF form or an excel sheet. These buttons are provided on the upper right corner of the screen.

### How  to add Trial Balance

			Print

	Modified on: Fri, 22 Jul, 2022 at 12:31 PM

		Location: Accounts Production > Client > Tasks > Trial Balance

Trial Balance is a bookkeeping worksheet in which the balances of all ledgers are compiled into debit and credit columns. A company prepares a trial balance periodically, usually at the end of every reporting period.

Once you are in the clients workspace under Tasks > Trial Balance, You can add/import a new trial balance by clicking on "+ Trial Balance".

Reference number of trial balance will be created by default  you can edit the reference as per your choice.

Description (if any) to be given to trial balance will come. 

Period of 12 months will be taken from the start date. Both of these dates are editable.

From and To are the dates for which trial balance is to be prepared will come. 

Mode of importing trial balance:

Bookkeeping

CSV Import

Manual Entry

QuickBooks Online Import

Xero Import

### Bookkeeping 

This will take the data from bookkeeping  under Capium for the company for which report is to be prepared. 

This option is suitable only for the clients whose bookkeeping is maintained.

### CSV Import

This option is used to import the ledgers and its balances in CSV format stored on the Local Computer.

### Manual Entry

You may create trial balance by selecting the manual option and clicking on ‘import/create’ tab.

A new page appears where the details of account ledgers and their balance are to be filled.

The new item can also be added by clicking on’ Add New Item’.

Once all the details are filled and the total of Debit and Credit are equal you may save it.

On saving, trial balance will be added to the list on the main page.

QuickBooks Online Import

You can directly import a Trial Balance from QuickBooks Online. Upon importing those entries, you will need to map the Trial Balance according to Capium's Chart of Accounts

Xero Import 

You can directly import a Trial Balance from Xero. Upon importing those entries, you will need to map the Trial Balance according to Capium's Chart of Accounts

### Submit

			Print

	Modified on: Mon, 24 Aug, 2020 at  5:04 PM

		Location: Accounts Production module > Client Specific > Tasks > Submit

This subsection is covers the process of submitting prepared Annual Reports to Companies House.

Only Abbreviated & Filleted reports can submitted to Companies House from Capium

When you click on Submit you will need to navigate through the 4 step process:

1. Validate Report (Pre-validation stage where you will be prompted if there are any issues)
2. Verify Report - you will be presented with the prepared accounts to review
3. Gateway Details - Enter your gateway details if this is your first submission
4. Submit to Companies House 

It shows the details of Reports submitted to Companies House containing:

Ref. No. of the report so submitted.

From and to date showing the dates for which trial balance was prepared and hence the report.

Type of report abbreviated or full with the name of the report in the description.

Date of submission to Companies House.

Status of submission

 - Pending: If the report has been submitted to Companies House but the response from Companies House is to be received.

 - Submitted: If the report has been submitted with the response received from Companies House.

 - Error: If there is an error after submission of the report then this status is shown.

### Actions that can be taken on the report submitted:

Download Report as PDF: Report so submitted can be downloaded as PDF.

 - Download Response as PDF: Response to be received from Companies House can be downloaded as PDF on receipt.

Quick link

Capium allows you to import an iXBRL report of Abbreviated accounts from other providers and then to submit to Companies House. To do this, head to the Submit page using the navigation above 

You need to fill in the details as per the requirement and upload the iXBRL file of abbreviated accounts from your system. Make sure that the ‘Accounting Period’ is the same as mentioned in the imported iXBRL report. Also, the ‘Directors Signing date in the pop-up and the iXBRL report should be the same.

Note: Capium will not perform any kind of validation check on the iXBRL set of accounts generated using other providers. Capium simply submits such iXBRL set of accounts to Companies House and allows the user to get the response, and will not rectify any generated errors in the submitted accounts. You can contact your iXBRL provider to resolve any errors received as a response by the Companies House.

The four step process for submission are as follows:

Validate Report: Annual report so generated is to be validated here. If there are any errors, then the same will be listed here and you may click on resolve to resolve the errors.

 - After resolving the errors, you will be allowed to proceed to the next step.

Verify Report: Report so generated is displayed. You may preview the Report which is to be submitted to Companies House. Also if you want to navigate to the previous step, you may click on the ‘Previous’ tab.

Gateway Details: Here details of Companies House login are to be filled. 

Submit Accounts: Once you are logged in to Companies House all the accounts and reports to be submitted is to be reviewed and then submitted to Companies House.

Important Note: To submit your accounts through an online accounting software, you must apply to Companies House to register and receive Gateway details.

If you have not yet applied for the online submission details, click on the following link of Companies House: https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/apply-for-a-companies-house-online-filing-presenter-account 

Mandatory information required while accounts submission:

While submitting accounts to Companies House through Capium or any other online accounting software, you need to have following Gateway details (Companies House Login details) handy:

Username/Presenter ID - Presenter ID is basically an 11-digit code which is issued by Companies House.

Password/Authentication Code – Authentication code issued by Companies House for filing company documents online including annual returns and dormant accounts. 

Company Authorisation ID – It specifies the company-specific unique 6 characters’ alphanumeric code issued by the Companies House.

Filing returns to Companies House as an Agent:

There is no provision for acting as an agent while filing returns for your clients to Companies House, it isn’t actually required. Accountants can use their own Presenter ID and Authentication Code while filing returns for their clients. But they should use Company Authentication Code of the specific company they are filing annual returns for. 

Your client or company should provide you with this code to make the submission on their behalf online.

To file accounts on behalf of your clients you will need the following details:

Username/Presenter ID - Accountant’s web filing Username, called Presenter ID.

Password/Authentication Code - Accountant’s web filing Password also called Authentication Code issued by Companies House for filing company returns online.

Company Authorisation ID/Company Authentication Code – It specifies unique 6 characters’ alphanumeric code issued by the Companies House for the company you are filing annual returns for, that is the one being submitted and not yours.

Note: We cannot guarantee that ibrxl accounts generated outside of Capium will be able to submitted with Capium.

These are the financial statements of the company which are the basis for reporting. This report is for submission to HMRC and Companies House. This section is about the preparation of Annual Report.

To create a report trial Balance is to be imported or created which acts as the base for generating Financial Statements.

Trial Balance is imported from the ‘Tasks’ section and then you need to follow the procedure as discussed in ‘Tasks’ section to import Trial Balance.

Then click on ‘+ Add New Report’. A new box appears for filling the basic credentials to create a report.

Adding New Report Section Details;

Ref. No. is generated by default and can be changed. By default, Prefix is ‘AA’ and numbered in sequence automatically.

The name to be given to the report (if any) can be given in description which will be displayed on the top of the report.

Report type is to be selected from drop down box as:

Annual Full Accounts: This type of Annual Report is used as an additional document (not mandatory) to be submitted with CT600 form in ‘CORPORATION TAX’ module of the software which is submitted to HMRC. It contains the complete details of Financial Statements (both Balance Sheet and Profit and Loss Account).

Annual Abbreviated Accounts: This type of Annual Report is submitted to Companies House. The contents of this report are similar to the Annual Full Accounts Report except that only Balance Sheet will form part of the report not Profit and Loss Account.

Trial Balance so imported will have to be selected. If previous year’s figures are to be shown, then put a tick on the checkbox of ‘Show Comparative Figures’ and select the Trial Balance whose figures are to be compared with current Trial balance.

Enter the Director and Accountant sign date for the report which will be shown in the report that will be generated.

Click on generate after mentioning all the fields. This will generate the report and preview of the report will appear on the screen.

After generating the preview report is to be saved by clicking on ‘Save Report’ tab. The report so saved will be added to the list of reports on the main page of this section.

		Companies House Login Changes – GOV.UK One Login from 13 October 2025

What’s Changing

From 13 October 2025, users will no longer be able to access Companies House WebFiling using the existing login methods, such as the Presenter ID.

Instead, all users will be required to sign in using a GOV.UK One Login.

This change is part of the government’s initiative to unify and strengthen login security across its online services.

Upon your first sign-in after this date, you will be redirected to connect your existing WebFiling account to your GOV.UK One Login.

If you don’t yet have a GOV.UK One Login, you’ll be guided through the process to create one.

For more details, visit the official GOV.UK announcement:

? Access to Companies House WebFiling accounts to move to GOV.UK One Login

### Does the GOV.UK One Login change affect software filing?

No — the switch to GOV.UK One Login only applies to Companies House WebFiling accounts (the manual, browser-based filing portal).

If you currently file documents via Capium or another Companies House-integrated software, you do not need to switch to GOV.UK One Login.

Software filing uses API credentials (the Presenter ID, Presenter Authentication Code, and Company Authentication Code) that are separate from WebFiling logins.These credentials remain valid and continue to be used for automated filings via software integrations.

### CIC Accounts Walkthough

			Print

	Modified on: Tue, 18 Aug, 2026 at  4:41 PM

This article walks you through the complete process of preparing and submitting accounts for a Community Interest Company (CIC) client in Capium, from importing the trial balance through to submitting your accounts to Companies House. It is intended for accountants and practice staff who have already added a CIC client to Accounts Production and are ready to begin the accounts preparation process.

### 
Before You Start

You will need a CIC client already set up in Accounts Production. If you have not yet added your CIC client, follow the separate article on adding a CIC client before continuing with this walkthrough.

Creating or a New CIC client
Converting an existing client to a CIC

### 
Step 1: Confirm Company Information

Navigation > Accounts Production > Select client > Settings > Report Settings > Company Info

Before doing anything else, check that the following information is correct:

Company registration number
CIC status has been correctly selected
General report information
If this CIC is being audited, select the audited option. If you need to disclose debtors due after more than one year in the balance sheet, select this option as well.

Click Save once you have confirmed everything is correct. This updates the company information used throughout the rest of the accounts.

### 
Step 2: Set Accounting Periods

Navigation > Accounts Production > Select client > Settings > Accounting Periods

Make sure both your current and previous accounting periods are showing. If a period is missing, click Add Accounting Period and save it.

You will only be able to select an accounting period in the trial balance section once it has been added here, so this step must be completed before importing your trial balance.

### 
Step 3: Import the Trial Balance

Navigation > Accounts Production > Select client > Tasks > Import Trial Balance

You can import your trial balance in one of the following ways:

From the Bookkeeping module
From QuickBooks or Xero
From FreeAgent
Using a CSV file
Once imported, these transactions form the basis of the accounts you will produce later in this process.

### 
Step 4: Update Company Contacts and Directors

Navigation > Accounts Production > Select client > Reports > Settings > Company Contacts

Check that all directors are showing correctly. If any directors are missing, click Update Companies House Directors to refresh the director list directly from Companies House.

### 
Step 5: Director's Report

Navigation > Accounts Production > Select client > Reports > Director's Report

Choose the director who will sign off the director's report and the balance sheet.

CICs require a second signature. When completing the CIC notes later in this process, you will be able to specify whether the same director is signing off the CIC declaration, or whether a different director should be selected.

### 
Step 6: Accountant's Report

Navigation > Accounts Production > Select client > Reports > Accountant's Report

Choose either a specific accountant within your firm or your firm's representation. You can also select the notes you want to include as the reporting accountant.

### 
Step 7: Accounting Policies

Navigation > Accounts Production > Select client > Reports > Accounting Policies

Select all accounting policies relevant to this company.

### 
Step 8: Additional Notes

Navigation > Accounts Production > Select client > Reports > Additional Notes

Click the green button to update the average number of employees for the period.

### 
Step 9: Customise Headers

Navigation > Accounts Production > Select client > Reports > Customise Headers

Make any changes needed to the headers used throughout the report.

### 
Step 10: CIC34 Notes

Navigation > Accounts Production > Select client > Reports > CIC34 Notes

The CIC34 note has six parts:

CIC impact and activities
Consultations with stakeholders
Directors' remuneration
Transfer of assets
Interest paid
Signatory (you can select the same or a different director here)
These sections are left blank by design. Capium does not pre-fill CIC34 notes, as the content is specific to each CIC and must reflect that company's actual activities and disclosures. Practices should complete all six parts directly to avoid compliance risk, do not leave these sections incomplete or rely on template wording carried over from another client.

### 
Step 11: Generate Annual Accounts

Navigation > Accounts Production > Select client > Reports > Annual Accounts

Produce the full set of annual accounts. This is required to send data through to the Corporation Tax module.

You will also need to produce either the abridged or filleted accounts, as this version is used to create the submission zip file for Companies House.

You must create both sets, full, and abridged or filleted, before continuing.

### 
Step 12: Generate the CIC Report

Navigation > Accounts Production > Select client > Reports > CIC Report

Click Add Report, choose the tax year you are reporting on, and click Generate. This produces the CIC report that will be merged with your accounts for submission.

### 

### Step 13: Create the Submission Zip Package

Navigation > Accounts Production > Select client > Tasks > CIC Submission Wizard

Click Create Zip Package, then:

Choose your accounts
Choose your CIC report
Click Generate Report
The system will run pre-validation checks on your documents. If any check fails, you will not be able to create the zip package until the issue is resolved.

Once pre-validation passes, click Proceed and Generate Zip File. The system will generate a downloadable file.

### 
Step 14: Submit to Companies House

Open the downloaded HTML file and click through to the Companies House to make your submission.

There is currently no direct submission route for CIC accounts within Capium. Submitting through the Government Gateway portal is the only way to complete this filing. You will need to submit this via the Companies House website, check the Companies House site directly for the latest submission requirements.

Once submitted, you can mark the task as complete within Capium.

Note: If you are setting up a brand new client as a CIC rather than converting an existing one, refer to this article.
### Before you start

The client must currently be set up in Capium as a Limited company type. Only limited company clients can be converted to a CIC.
You will need access to the My Admin module.
Review the client's existing record before you start, so you can identify any of the fields below that are missing or out of date.

### Converting the client

Confirm the client type is set to Limited company. 
Select the option to designate the client as a CIC. 
Review and update the client's details. 
Save the client record.

### Option 2: converting via Accounts Production report settings

You can also convert a client to a CIC from within Accounts Production, at the point where you are setting up the client's report settings. This is useful if you are already working on the client's accounts and want to enable CIC status without leaving Accounts Production.

Navigate to the client's report settings. Navigation > Accounts Production > Select Client > Settings > Report Settings > Company Info
Select Edit at the bottom of the screen to make changes.

	Modified on: Mon, 17 Aug, 2026 at  1:32 PM

		The CIC 34 Notes hold the content of the CIC 34 report. The report is built entirely from these notes, so anything left blank in the notes will be blank in the report.

This is the second step in the CIC filing process. For the full sequence, see CIC Filings in Accounts Production.

### 
Before you start

The CIC option must already be ticked against the client. If CIC 34 Notes does not appear under Settings, see Enabling the CIC option for a client.

### How to open the notes

Navigation > Accounts Production > Select a client > Settings > CIC 34 Notes

Open the client in Accounts Production.
Go to Settings, then CIC 34 Notes.
Work through each of the six parts in turn.
Edit and save each part individually.
All fields are empty by default. Each part is saved on its own, so completing one part does not save the others. Mandatory fields show a validation error if you try to save the part while they are blank.

### 
The six parts

PartWhat it coversWhat you enter1General description of the company's activities and impactFree text describing the activities carried out during the year and how they benefited the community. Mandatory. The part cannot be saved while this is blank.2Consultation with stakeholdersYes or No. Selecting No inserts a default statement automatically. Selecting Yes unlocks three mandatory boxes: who the stakeholders are, how they were consulted, and what actions were taken as a result.3Directors' remunerationIf the detail is already disclosed in the additional notes of the accounts, tick the confirmation box and enter the reference. If not, enter directors' emoluments, benefits in kind in aggregate, compensation for loss of office, benefits provided to third parties for directors' services, and the number of directors benefiting under each type of retirement benefit scheme, for the current and prior year.4Transfer of assets other than for full considerationEnter each asset in the table provided along with its estimated fair value. Assets transferred at full value are not entered here. Additional narrative is optional.5Interest paid at a performance related rateYes or No. Selecting No inserts a default statement. Selecting Yes unlocks a description of the borrowing, the effective interest rate and the interest cap value. If the effective rate is above the cap, a reason is also required. The method used to determine the rate is optional.6SignatoryThe date of signing and the name of the director signing the report.
### Points to be aware of

Write the content as it should read on the filed report rather than as an internal working note. The text is used exactly as entered.
The notes cover the current financial year only. There is no comparative content and no prior year version of the notes to complete.
Nothing is populated from the trial balance or from the annual accounts. Every part is entered manually.
Empty notes do not stop the report generating. Capium will produce the CIC 34 report with those parts blank, which is why the notes must be finished before you generate the report.

			Print

	Modified on: Thu, 20 Aug, 2026 at 12:56 PM

		Once your CIC accounts and CIC 34 report have been prepared, you can generate a submission zip package ready for filing with Companies House.

Navigation: Accounts Production > Select client > Tasks > CIC Submission Wizard

### 
Before you start
Make sure the following have been completed:

 - Your CIC accounts have been prepared and finalised.
 - Your CIC 34 report has been generated.

### 

### Steps

 - From the CIC Submission Wizard, click Create Zip Package.
 - Choose your accounts.
 - Choose your CIC report.
 - Click Generate Report.

The system will run pre-validation checks on your documents. If any check fails, you will not be able to create the zip package until the issue has been resolved.

 - Once pre-validation passes, click Proceed and Generate Zip File.

The system will generate a downloadable file. This file must be submitted to Companies House manually via the Government Gateway, as there is currently no in-app submission route for CIC filings.
